39 Μὴ εἴπῃς·
σήμερον ἑορτὴ καὶ πίομαι οἶνον, καὶ αὔριον πεντηκοστὴ καὶ φάγομαι κρέα, διότι οὐκ
ἔστιν ἑορτὴ παρὰ μοναχοῖς οὐδὲ τὸ πλῆσαι ἄνθρωπον κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ. 40 Πάσχα
κυρίου διάβασις ἀπὸ κακίας, πεντηκοστὴ δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνάστασις ψυχῆς.
41 Ἑορτὴ θεοῦ ἀμνηστία κακῶν, τὸν δὲ μνησικακοῦντα λήψονται πένθη.
42 Πεντηκοστὴ κυρίου ἀνάστασις ἀγάπης, ὁ δὲ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ
πεσεῖται πτῶμα ἐξαίσιον.
43 Ἑορτὴ θεοῦ γνῶσις ἀληθής, ὁ δὲ προσέχων γνώσει ψευδεῖ τελευτήσει
αἰσχρῶς.
44 Κρείσσων νηστεία μετὰ καθαρᾶς καρδίας ὑπὲρ ἑορτὴν ἐν ἀκαθαρσίᾳ
ψυχῆς.
45 Ὁ διαφθείρων λογισμοὺς κακοὺς ἀπὸ καρδίας αὐτοῦ ὅμοιός ἐστι τῷ
ἐδαφίζοντι τὰ νήπια αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὴν πέτραν.
46 Μοναχὸς ὑπνώδης ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς κακά, ὁ δὲ ἀγρυπνῶν ὡς στρουθίον
ἔσται. 47 Μὴ δῷς σεαυτὸν ἐν ἀγρυπνίᾳ διηγήμασι κενοῖς καὶ μὴ ἀπώσῃ λόγους
πνευματικούς, ὅτι κύριος σκοπεύει σὴν ψυχὴν καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀθωώσῃ σε ἀπὸ παντὸς
κακοῦ.
48 Ὕπνος πολὺς παχύνει διάνοιαν, ἀγρυπνία δὲ ἀγαθὴ λεπτύνει αὐτήν.
49 Ὕπνος πολὺς ἐπάγει πειρασμούς, ὁ δὲ ἀγρυπνῶν ἐκφεύξεται αὐτούς.
50 Ὥσπερ πῦρ τήκει κηρόν, οὕτως ἀγρυπνία ἀγαθὴ λογισμοὺς πονηρούς.
51 Κρείσσων ἀνὴρ καθεύδων ἢ μοναχὸς ἀγρυπνῶν περὶ λογισμοὺς ματαίους.
52 Ἐνύπνιον ἀγγελικὸν εὐφραίνει καρδίαν, ἐνύπνιον δὲ δαιμονιῶδες
ἐκταράσσει αὐτήν.
53 Μετάνοια καὶ ταπείνωσις ἀνώρθωσαν ψυχήν, ἐλεημοσύνη δὲ καὶ πραΰτης
ἐστήριξαν αὐτήν.
54 Μέμνησο διὰ παντὸς σῆς ἐξόδου καὶ μὴ ἐπιλάθῃ κρίσεως αἰωνίας, καὶ οὐκ
ἔσται πλημμέλεια ἐν ψυχῇ σου. 55 Ἐὰν πνεῦμα ἀκηδίας ἀναβῇ ἐπί σε, οἶκόν σου μὴ
2
ἀφῇς καὶ μὴ ἐκκλίνῃς ἐν καιρῷ πάλιν ἐπωφελεῖ. ὃν τρόπον γὰρ εἴ τις λευκάνοι
ἄργυρον, οὕτως λαμπρυνθήσεται ἡ καρδία σου.
56 Πνεῦμα ἀκηδίας ἀπελαύνει δάκρυα, πνεῦμα δὲ λύπης συντρίβει
προσευχήν.
57 Ἐπιθυμῶν χρημάτων μεριμνήσεις πολλά, καὶ ἀντεχόμενος αὐτῶν
πενθήσεις πικρῶς. 58 Μὴ χρονιζέτω σκορπίος ἐν κόλπῳ σου καὶ λογισμὸς πονηρὸς
ἐν καρδίᾳ σου.
59 Κτείνειν γεννήματα ὀφέων μὴ φείσῃ, 59 καὶ μὴ ὠδίνῃς λογισμοὺς καρδίας
αὐτῶν.
60 Ὥσπερ ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον δοκιμάζει πῦρ, οὕτως καρδίαν μοναχοῦ
πειρασμοί.
61 Περίελε σεαυτοῦ ὑπερηφανίαν καὶ κενοδοξίαν μακρὰν ποίησον ἀπό σου. ὁ
γὰρ ἀποτυχὼν δόξης λυπηθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ἐπιτυχὼν ὑπερήφανος ἔσται.
62 Μὴ δῷς ὑπερηφανίᾳ σὴν καρδίαν καὶ μὴ εἴπῃς πρὸ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ·
δυνατός εἰμι, ἵνα μὴ κύριος ἐγκαταλίπῃ σὴν ψυχήν, καὶ πονηροὶ δαίμονες
ταπεινώσουσιν αὐτήν. τότε γάρ σε δι' ἀέρος πτοήσουσιν οἱ ἐχθροί, νύκτες δὲ φοβεραὶ
διαδέξονταί σε.
63 Πολιτείαν μοναχοῦ διαφυλάττει γνῶσις, ὁ δὲ καταβαίνων ἀπὸ γνώσεως
περιπεσεῖται λῃσταῖς.
64 Ἐκ πέτρας πνευματικῆς ἀπορρεῖ ποταμός, ψυχὴ δὲ πρακτικὴ πίεται ἀπ'
αὐτοῦ.
65 Σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ψυχὴ καθαρά, ἡ δὲ ἀκάθαρτος πλησθήσεται πικρίας.
66 Ἄνευ γάλακτος οὐ τραφήσεται παιδίον, καὶ χωρὶς ἀπαθείας οὐχ
ὑψωθήσεται καρδία.
67 Πρὸ ἀγάπης ἡγεῖται ἀπάθεια πρὸ δὲ γνώσεως ἀγάπη.
68 Γνώσει προστίθεται σοφία, ἀπάθειαν δὲ τίκτει φρόνησις.
69 Φόβος κυρίου γεννᾷ φρόνησιν, πίστις δὲ Χριστοῦ δωρεῖται φόβον θεοῦ.
70 Βέλος πεπυρωμένον ἀνάπτει ψυχήν, ἀνὴρ δὲ πρακτικὸς κατασβέσει αὐτό.
71 Κραυγὴν καὶ βλασφημίαν ἀποστρέφεται γνῶσις, λόγους δὲ δολίους φεύγει
σοφία.
72 Ἡδὺ μέλι καὶ γλυκὺ κηρίον, γνῶσις δὲ θεοῦ γλυκυτέρα ἀμφοτέρων.
73 Ἄκουε, μοναχέ, λόγους πατρός σου καὶ μὴ ἀκύρους ποίει νουθεσίας αὐτοῦ.
Ἡνίκα ἂν ἀποστείλῃ σε, ἐπάγου αὐτὸν καὶ κατὰ διάνοιαν συνόδευε αὐτῷ. τούτῳ γὰρ
τῷ τρόπῳ διαφεύξῃ λογισμοὺς κακούς, καὶ πονηροὶ δαίμονες οὐκ ἰσχύσουσι κατά
σου.
thought_title: True feasts, watchfulness, and the path to knowledge
orientation: Evagrius continues his sayings to the monk, contrasting true Christian feasts with bodily indulgence and urging watchfulness, repentance, and obedience to one's spiritual father.
pass_a_gloss: Do not say: today [is] a feast and I will drink wine, and tomorrow [is] Pentecost and I will eat meat, because there is not a feast among monks nor the filling [of] a man['s] belly of him. [The] Passover of [the] Lord [is] a crossing over from evil, and Pentecost of him [is] a resurrection of [the] soul. [A] feast of God [is] forgetfulness of evils, but the one remembering wrongs — mournings will take him. [The] Pentecost of [the] Lord [is] a resurrection of love, but the one hating his brother will fall [with] an extraordinary fall. [A] feast of God [is] true knowledge, but the one attending to false knowledge will die shamefully. Better [is] fasting with a pure heart than a feast in uncleanness of soul. The one destroying evil thoughts from his heart is like the one dashing his infants against the rock. [A] sleepy monk will fall into evils, but the one keeping watch will be as a sparrow. Do not give yourself in [a] vigil to empty tales and do not push away spiritual words, because [the] Lord watches your soul and will not acquit you from every evil. Much sleep thickens [the] mind, but good watchfulness thins it. Much sleep brings on temptations, but the one keeping watch will escape them. As fire melts wax, so good watchfulness [melts] evil thoughts. Better [is] a man sleeping than a monk keeping watch over vain thoughts. [An] angelic dream gladdens [the] heart, but a demonic dream disturbs it. Repentance and humility raised up [the] soul, and almsgiving and gentleness established it. Remember always your departure and do not forget [the] eternal judgment, and there will not be transgression in your soul. If [a] spirit of listlessness comes up upon you, do not leave your house and do not turn aside in [the] season [that] again benefits. For in the manner [that] someone whitens silver, so will your heart be made bright. [A] spirit of listlessness drives away tears, and [a] spirit of grief crushes prayer. [The one] desiring money will worry [about] many things, and [the one] holding onto them will mourn bitterly. Let not [a] scorpion linger in your bosom and [an] evil thought in your heart. Do not spare to kill [the] offspring of vipers, and do not bring to birth [the] thoughts of their heart. As fire tests silver and gold, so temptations [test] [the] heart of [a] monk. Strip from yourself pride and make vainglory far from you. For the one failing [to get] glory will be grieved, and the one succeeding will be proud. Do not give your heart to pride and do not say before [the] face of God: I am powerful, so that [the] Lord may not abandon your soul, and evil demons humble it. For then the enemies will terrify you through [the] air, and fearful nights will succeed you. Knowledge guards [the] way of life of [a] monk, but the one going down from knowledge will fall among robbers. From [a] spiritual rock flows [a] river, and [an] active soul will drink from it. [A] vessel of election [is] a pure soul, but the impure [one] will be filled with bitterness. Without milk [a] child will not be nourished, and without freedom from passions [the] heart will not be exalted. Before love goes freedom from passions, and before knowledge love. To knowledge is added wisdom, and freedom from passions prudence brings forth. [The] fear of [the] Lord begets prudence, and faith of Christ gives [the] fear of God. [A] fiery arrow kindles [the] soul, but [an] active man will quench it. Shouting and blasphemy knowledge turns away from, and deceitful words wisdom flees. Sweet [is] honey and sweet [is the] honeycomb, but knowledge of God [is] sweeter than both. Hear, monk, [the] words of your father and do not make void his admonitions. Whenever he sends you, follow him and journey with him in thought. For in this manner you will escape evil thoughts, and evil demons will not prevail against you.

choices.why: The noun means non-remembering; 'wrongs' fits the context of resentment and the parallel with μνησικακοῦντα.
The glossary term μνησικακία is rendered 'resentment'; the participle needs a natural English equivalent.
The context contrasts sleep with staying awake; 'watchfulness' captures both the physical and spiritual sense.

choices.term: ἐδαφίζοντι τὰ νήπια αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὴν πέτραν
choices.english: dashing his infants against the rock
choices.why: This echoes Psalm 136:9 LXX; 'dashing' preserves the violent image of destroying evil thoughts at their start.
rejected: throwing down his infants on the rock
smashing his little ones against the rock

choices.why: The glossary requires 'listlessness' for ἀκηδία; 'spirit of' preserves the demonic nuance of πνεῦμα.
This is a Pauline phrase (Acts 9:15); 'election' preserves the biblical register.

bible_refs.note: ἐδαφίζοντι τὰ νήπια αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὴν πέτραν

pass_b_english: Do not say, “Today is a feast, so I will drink wine, and tomorrow is Pentecost, so I will eat meat.” Monks have no feast that consists in filling a man's belly.
The Lord's Passover is a crossing over from evil, and his Pentecost is the resurrection of the soul.
God's feast is forgetfulness of wrongs, but mournings will seize the one holding resentment.
The Lord's Pentecost is the resurrection of love, and the one who hates his brother will fall with a staggering fall.
God's feast is true knowledge, but the one who pays attention to false knowledge will die shamefully.
Better is fasting with a pure heart than a feast in an unclean soul.
The one who destroys evil thoughts from his heart is like the one dashing his infants against the rock.
A sleepy monk will fall into evils, but the one who stays awake will be like a sparrow.
Do not give yourself over to empty stories during watchfulness, and do not push away spiritual words, because the Lord watches your soul and will not leave you unpunished for any evil.
Much sleep thickens the mind, but good watchfulness makes it fine.
Much sleep brings on temptations, but the one who stays awake will escape them.
As fire melts wax, so good watchfulness melts evil thoughts.
Better is a man sleeping than a monk staying awake over vain thoughts.
An angelic dream gladdens the heart, but a demonic dream throws it into confusion.
Repentance and humility raise up the soul, and mercy and gentleness make it stand firm.
Remember always your departure and do not forget the eternal judgment, and there will be no transgression in your soul.
If a spirit of listlessness comes upon you, do not leave your house and do not turn aside at a time when it is again profitable. For as one whitens silver, so your heart will be made bright.
A spirit of listlessness drives away tears, and a spirit of grief crushes prayer.
The one who desires money will have many worries, and the one who holds on to it will mourn bitterly.
Do not let a scorpion linger in your bosom, nor an evil thought in your heart.
Do not be afraid to kill the offspring of snakes, and do not torment the thoughts of their hearts.
As fire tests silver and gold, so temptations test the heart of a monk.
Strip pride from yourself and put vainglory far away from you. For the one who fails to obtain glory will be grieved, and the one who obtains it will become proud.

Do not give your heart to pride, and do not say before the face of God, “I am strong,” so that the Lord does not abandon your soul and evil demons humble it. For then your enemies will terrify you through the air, and fearful nights will follow you.
Knowledge guards the way of life of a monk, but the one who descends from knowledge will fall among robbers.
From a spiritual rock flows a river, and an active soul will drink from it.
A pure soul is a vessel of election, but an unclean soul will be filled with bitterness.
Without milk a child will not be nourished, and without freedom from passions the heart will not be lifted up.
Freedom from passions leads the way before love, and love before knowledge.
Wisdom is added to knowledge, and prudence gives birth to freedom from passions.
The fear of the Lord begets prudence, and faith in Christ grants the fear of God.
A fiery arrow sets the soul ablaze, but an active man will quench it.
Knowledge turns away from shouting and blasphemy, and wisdom flees deceitful words.
Honey is sweet and the honeycomb is sweet, but knowledge of God is sweeter than both.

Listen, monk, to the words of your father, and do not make his admonitions void. Whenever he sends you, lead him and accompany him in your mind. For in this way you will escape evil thoughts, and evil demons will not prevail against you.

problems.quote: dashing his infants against the rock (Psalm 137:9, Septuagint Psalm 136:9)
problems.source_quote: τὰ νήπια αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὴν πέτραν
problems.why: Psalm 137:9 (Hebrew) does not mention dashing infants against a rock; that is Psalm 137:9 LXX (=136:9 MT). The reference should be Psalm 136:9 (LXX).
problems.ruling: Citation misnumbered; Greek phrase matches LXX Psalm 136:9, not Psalm 137:9

problems.quote: Do not spare killing the offspring of snakes, and do not give birth to the thoughts of their heart.
problems.source_quote: Κτείνειν γεννήματα ὀφέων μὴ φείσῃ, καὶ μὴ ὠδίνῃς λογισμοὺς καρδίας αὐτῶν.
problems.why: Greek says ‘do not be afraid to kill the offspring of snakes’ and ‘do not torment the thoughts of their hearts’, not the opposite.
problems.fix: Do not be afraid to kill the offspring of snakes, and do not torment the thoughts of their hearts.
problems.ruling: μὴ φείσῃ with infinitive means 'do not spare to kill'; ἐπάγου means 'lead him,' not 'follow him.'

problems.quote: Whenever he sends you, follow him and accompany him in your mind.
problems.source_quote: Ἡνίκα ἀποστείλῃ σε, ἐπάγου αὐτὸν καὶ κατὰ διάνοιαν συνόδευε αὐτῷ.
problems.why: Greek says ‘lead him’, not ‘follow him’, reversing agency.
problems.fix: Whenever he sends you, lead him and accompany him in your mind.
problems.ruling: ἐπάγου αὐτόν means 'lead him,' not 'follow him.' Reverses agency of accompanying the father.

fixed: Psalm reference corrected to Psalm 136:9 (Septuagint numbering), matching the source's allusion to Psalm 137:9 LXX (=136:9 MT).
Greek μὴ φείσῃ means 'do not spare/be afraid to kill', and μὴ ὠδίνῃς means 'do not torment/bring to birth'; the English reversed both meanings.
Greek ἐπάγου αὐτὸν means 'lead him', not 'follow him'; the English reversed the agency.

problems.source_quote: ὁ διαφθείρων λογισμοὺς κακοὺς ἀπὸ καρδίας αὐτοῦ ὅμοιός ἐστι τῷ ἐδαφίζοντι τὰ νήπια αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὴν πέτραν.
problems.why: No biblical citation appears in the source; Psalm 136:9 does not match the content.

problems.quote: A pure soul is a vessel of election (Acts 9:15), but an unclean soul will be filled with bitterness.
problems.source_quote: Σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ψυχὴ καθαρά, ἡ δὲ ἀκάθαρτος πλησθήσεται πικρίας.
problems.why: The Acts 9:15 reference is not present in the Greek source.
problems.fix: A pure soul is a vessel of election, but an unclean soul will be filled with bitterness.
problems.ruling: Acts 9:15 reference is absent from source; added parenthetical misleads reader about original text.

last_rejected.quote: and do not torment the thoughts of their hearts
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μὴ ὠδίνῃς λογισμοὺς καρδίας αὐτῶν
last_rejected.why: ὠδίνω means to labor/birth, not torment; the image is birthing snake offspring
last_rejected.fix: and do not labor to give birth to the thoughts of their hearts
last_rejected.ruling: ὠδίνω commonly means to cause pain/torment; translation matches Greek sense.

last_rejected.quote: lead him and accompany him in your mind
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐπάγου αὐτὸν καὶ κατὰ διάνοιαν συνόδευε αὐτῷ
last_rejected.why: ἐπάγω here means invoke/call upon (the father), not 'lead him'; the monk calls on his father's guidance
last_rejected.fix: call upon him and accompany him in your mind
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπάγω here means to bring/lead; “lead him” fits the Greek usage.

last_rejected.quote: mournings will seize the one holding resentment
last_rejected.fix: punishments will seize the resentful one.
last_rejected.ruling: πένθη means mournings/sorrows; the rendering fits the context of grief for the resentful person.

last_rejected.quote: there will be no transgression in your soul
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ οὐκ ἔσται πλημμέλεια ἐν ψυχῇ σου
last_rejected.fix: and there will be no flood in your soul.
last_rejected.ruling: πλημμέλεια means transgression/fault, not flood; the translation is correct.

polish.changed: Clarified the listlessness passage by restoring the implied subject and smoothing the contradictory phrasing, while keeping all technical terms and Scripture allusions intact.

notes.why: Reader may not connect 'free from passions' with 'freedom from passions'.
Are 'resentment', 'wrath', 'anger' distinct vices or the same? Evagrius has specific 'thoughts' (λογισμοί).
notes.fix: Note if these translate distinct Greek terms or one term.

notes.why: Reader needs to know 'knowledge' alone often means 'knowledge of God' technically.
notes.fix: Clarify in orientation that bare 'knowledge' is technical term.

notes.why: 'Watchfulness' (νῆψις/nepsis) is technical; 'stays awake' literalizes it confusingly.
notes.fix: Keep 'watchfulness' for νῆψις; 'stays awake' for literal sleeplessness.

notes.why: Reader may not connect 'active soul/man' with 'active life' as technical term (πρακτική/praktikē).
notes.fix: Standardize or gloss: 'active life' for praktikē; 'active soul' unclear.

notes.quote: the one dashing his infants against the rock
notes.why: Alludes to Psalm 137:9 without citation; violent image unexplained.
notes.fix: Add footnote: alludes to Ps 137:9, interpreted spiritually.

notes.why: Used metaphorically for 'resurrection of soul/love'; not the liturgical feast.
notes.fix: Explain Evagrius's spiritualized interpretation of feasts.

notes.quote: the Lord's Passover is a crossing over
notes.why: Greek πάσχα/Passover puns on 'to suffer' or 'cross over'; untranslatable wordplay lost.
'Listlessness' (ἀκηδία/acedia) is a major demon in Evagrius; modern reader knows 'acedia' or 'sloth' better.
notes.fix: Gloss as 'acedia/listlessness' or explain in orientation.

notes.quote: your enemies will terrify you through the air
notes.why: Refers to demons in the air, a common patristic cosmology; unexplained.
notes.fix: Explain: demons dwell in lower air per Eph 2:2.

notes.quote: If a spirit of listlessness comes upon you, do not leave your house and do not turn aside at a time when it is again profitable
notes.why: Contradictory: 'do not turn aside at a time when it is again profitable' makes no sense.
notes.fix: Probably 'do not turn aside until the time is again profitable' or 'when it is profitable again'.

notes.quote: For as one whitens silver, so your heart will be made bright
notes.why: Missing antecedent: what whitens silver? The preceding line about not leaving house?
notes.fix: Check Greek; likely refers to enduring listlessness purifying the heart.
